mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign corporate shareholder of the planned WFOE
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry / registrar of companies in the foreign shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Step 1: notarize the original in the issuing jurisdiction. Step 2A: if the issuing jurisdiction is a Hague Apostille Convention member, obtain a single Hague Apostille from that jurisdiction's designated Competent Authority. Step 2B: if the issuing jurisdiction is not a member, obtain certification from the home Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then consular legalization at the People's Republic of China Embassy or Consulate in that jurisdiction. Routes 2A and 2B are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain them sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All natural-person UBOs, directors, supervisors, senior managers and authorized agents of the WFOE must undergo continuous negative-news and sanctions screening before incorporation and quarterly thereafter against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN sectoral sanctions, EU and UK OFSI consolidated financial sanctions lists, China's PBOC and SAMR compliance blacklists, the PRC public security counter-terrorism watchlist, and World Bank debarment lists; politically exposed persons (PEPs), their immediate family members and close associates require enhanced due diligence with senior-management sign-off, independent source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, ongoing transaction monitoring, and re-screening every 90 days; any OFAC, UN, EU, UK or domestic hit or PEP red flag must be escalated as a suspicious activity/transaction report and causes suspension of the proposed WFOE relationship until full legal clearance is obtained.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and its online enterprise name reservation module (State Administration for Market Regulation / local SAMR branch)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered head name of the WFOE must be in simplified Chinese characters only and must follow the four-tier naming structure: administrative division + trade name + industry description + organizational form, ending with Limited Liability Company. The trade name may be a pinyin transliteration of the foreign parent's name, but Latin script, standalone foreign words and numerical or typographic symbols are not permitted as substitutes for the statutory Chinese name; a supplementary English name may be recorded after incorporation but cannot replace the Chinese head name. The name must avoid false or misleading content, maintain consistency with the approved business scope, and be cleared for trademark conflicts before submission.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation granted by SAMR is valid for 30 days and is not administratively extendable; if the WFOE is not incorporated within that window, the applicant must submit a new name-clearance application. If the name is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration petition with the immediately higher-level SAMR within 60 days of receiving the written refusal, attaching the rejection notice, the proposed name, the legal basis for use, trademark search evidence and the business scope explanation. If the higher-level SAMR confirms the rejection, the applicant may bring an administrative lawsuit in a competent people's court within six months. As a practical protective measure, the initial filing should include two or three backup name variants so the incorporation timeline is not blocked.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure letter-box virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable as the sole registered address for a China WFOE in the simulated social-casino and virtual-slots software sector. Local SAMR requires a lawful commercial address evidenced by a lease, property certificate or government-authorized incubation agreement; tax authorities will reject VAT and corporate income tax registration if no physical business location exists; and banks uniformly decline corporate account opening when KYC site inspection cannot be completed. Premium serviced offices or government-endorsed incubator addresses may be acceptable in some free-trade zones if the landlord supports SAMR registration, tax inspection and mail receipt, but the entity should still maintain a dedicated office, staff, equipment and records at that location. For this industry, given reliance on Apple IAP and Google Play Billing and the intangible revenue stream, tax and bank scrutiny is elevated, so a virtual-office-only arrangement is operationally unviable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 45% within the first 18 months after registration, rising if the company files electronic-only invoices or has no visible staff on site. Checklist for inspection readiness: (1) company name board displayed at the registered entrance; (2) original registered office lease or property certificate; (3) financial records, ledgers, vouchers and invoices stored locally; (4) corporate contracts with foreign parent and platform partners; (5) software development evidence, server or cloud hosting agreements, and Apple/Google developer accounts; (6) UBO and AML screening files for all directors, supervisors and senior managers; (7) payroll, social insurance and employment records; (8) corporate seals and statutory books; (9) regulatory notice board and liaison contact; (10) staff availability for unannounced face-to-face interview by municipal tax or SAMR inspectors.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision), effective July 1, 2024, Articles 4, 6, 23, 33, 35, 41, 43-47, 57-60, 67-76; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 2, 4, 28-31; Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Registration Administration of Companies, Articles 2, 8, 19, 22 and 24-26; Foreign Investment Negative List (2023 edition) for market entry restrictions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local Market Regulation Administration (SAMR) at the district or municipal level where the registered office is located, acting through the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform and the SAMR enterprise registration window.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Application Form for Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company, filed together with the Articles of Association, the Pre-Approved Name Notice, registered address proof, and investor identity documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. PRC law imposes no statutory minimum registered capital and no blocked escrow account requirement for an ordinary wholly foreign-owned limited liability company in the software publishing sector. The Articles of Association must state a registered capital figure and a contribution schedule; under Article 47 of the Companies Law, all subscribed capital must be paid in full within five years from the date of issuance of the business license. Contributions may be made in cash or lawful non-monetary property and must be recorded in the company's capital contribution register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF CN_WFOE_LTD

WHEREAS, the sole shareholder has determined to incorporate the Company as a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company under the Companies Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision) and the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China, has approved the Articles of Association, and has appointed the undersigned first directors to serve until the first shareholders' meeting;

NOW, THEREFORE, THE BOARD RESOLVES AS FOLLOWS:

1. Share Capital Subscription. The registered capital of the Company shall be RMB 1,000,000, divided into 1,000,000 ordinary shares with a par value of RMB 1.00 each. The entire registered capital is subscribed by the sole shareholder. The Board adopts the capital contribution schedule and directs the General Manager to record all subscriptions in the share register, deliver share certificates, and ensure that each contribution is fully paid within five years from the date of issuance of the business license in accordance with Article 47 of the Companies Law. Contributions may be made in cash or lawful non-monetary assets; cash contributions shall be paid into a capital verification account at a licensed bank.

2. Registered Office. The registered office of the Company shall be at the address stated in the Articles of Association within the People's Republic of China. The Board approves such office as the Company's statutory seat and authorizes the Legal Representative to execute or negotiate any lease, sublease, utility or service agreement, to register the address with the local Market Regulation Administration, and to receive all official correspondence and legal process there.

3. Banking Authorization. The Board authorizes the General Manager and the Chief Financial Officer to open, with any licensed commercial bank in the People's Republic of China, a basic RMB settlement account, a foreign exchange settlement account, and such other banking facilities as are needed. The Bank is authorized to honor instructions from the Legal Representative and the Chief Financial Officer, singly for routine transactions up to RMB 200,000, and jointly for transactions above that amount, provided that total drawdowns are approved in the annual budget. The Board ratifies any such account opening already made and authorizes the filing of all foreign direct investment foreign exchange registrations with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange.

4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The Board appoints the person named in the filed registration as Chairman of the Board and Legal Representative, appoints the person named in the registration as General Manager and Chief Operating Officer, and appoints the person named in the registration as Supervisor. The Legal Representative shall file the company registration, sign all regulatory declarations, and represent the Company before government agencies. The General Manager shall exercise day-to-day management authority. The Supervisor shall independently oversee financial discipline and legal compliance as required by law.

5. General Authority and Effectiveness. The Board authorizes the Legal Representative and the General Manager, acting singly, to execute and deliver all documents, notices, powers of attorney, and certificates that any governmental, banking, or commercial counterparty may reasonably require to carry out this resolution. This resolution is adopted by unanimous written consent of all directors and is effective immediately, retroactively to the date of the Company's incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise Name Pre-Approval and Foreign Investment Pre-Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Regulation Administration (SAMR) enterprise registration window / National Integrated Online Government Service Platform (www.gov.cn)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online pre-filing through the SAMR enterprise registration portal for the proposed WFOE name and foreign investment information. The foreign parent must apply using its notarized certificate of incorporation and a board resolution appointing the local authorized representative. The proposed company name must include the administrative division, unique trade name, industry classification, and the words Limited Liability Company. Check the Foreign Investment Negative List; if any activity is restricted, the required approval must be obtained before filing. After name pre-approval, the pre-approved name notice is retained for six months. Use a Chinese-language version of the Articles of Association as controlling, and keep an English translation for the foreign parent.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership proof for registered address
Notarized certificate of incorporation or passport of foreign investor
Board resolution of foreign investor appointing local representative
Power of attorney in favor of local filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the pre-approval is queried, correct the online form and resubmit within ten working days; if the name is rejected, select an alternate name; if the negative list check identifies a restricted item, amend the business scope or obtain the relevant approval from MIIT or NDRC before continuing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Formal Company Incorporation Application and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Regulation Administration (SAMR) service hall or online enterprise registration system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Company Establishment Registration Application Form, the signed Articles of Association, the pre-approved name notice, proof of registered office, investor qualification documents, and identification of directors, supervisors and legal representative. The SAMR will review legal compliance, check the Foreign Investment Negative List, verify the business scope, and issue the business license bearing the unified social credit code. If the electronic platform is used, upload scanned originals certified by the foreign shareholder and pay no state registration fee. After issuance, SAMR automatically shares data with tax, social insurance, customs and statistics agencies under the multi-license integration reform. The WFOE must then complete post-registration filings with the tax and social insurance authorities.
required_dossiers: Articles of Association signed by the sole shareholder
Investor qualification documents and powers of attorney
Identification documents of legal representative, directors, supervisors and general manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration officer issues a query, respond through the online platform or service window within fifteen days with revised signatures or documents. If the authority refuses registration, the applicant may request administrative reconsideration before the next-level SAMR within sixty days or bring administrative litigation within six months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Seal Carving, Tax Registration, Social Insurance and Foreign Investment Reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau recognized seal engraving station; local State Taxation Administration office; Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; local commerce department reporting system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receiving the business license, carve the company seal, finance seal, legal representative seal and invoice seal at a public security approved engraving station; all seal impressions are recorded in the PSB database. Then complete tax registration through the Electronic Tax Bureau, register social insurance and housing fund, and file labor contracts for employees. The company must also submit its foreign investment operating status and updated information to the local commerce department through the Foreign Investment Information Reporting System within thirty days after incorporation. Keep board minutes and capital contribution records for corporate governance compliance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or social security registration encounters a mismatch, use the e-tax bureau correction function, file the correct information and supporting identity documents, and pay any late filing penalty if assessed; if the seal record fails, ask the engraving station to correct and update the PSB record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, SAFE Foreign Exchange Registration and Paid-In Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in the People's Republic of China; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through the bank's capital project information system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Take the original business license, company seal, Articles of Association, board resolution on banking authorization, and legal representative identity to the selected bank to open the basic deposit account. Use the bank to complete the SAFE Foreign Exchange Business registration for foreign direct investment; the bank will submit the capital project information and issue the FDI registration code. After the parent overseas wires the paid-in capital, the bank verifies the purpose, converts RMB, and deposits the funds into the capital account. Maintain the capital contribution verification record and file annual financial statements with SAMR. The banking process requires a beneficial ownership declaration and local address due diligence.
required_dossiers: Original business license and company seal
Legal representative identity document and power of attorney
SAFE foreign direct investment basic registration form
Bank account application forms and tax identification document
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or SAFE rejects the registration due to incomplete beneficial ownership or source-of-funds evidence, provide the bank with certified constitutional documents, bank statements showing the source of the remittance, and an updated board resolution; the bank must reassess under anti-money laundering rules; if unresolved, escalate to the local SAFE branch.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Records and Digital Content Compliance Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR annual report system; Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT); National Press and Publication Administration (NPPA); China Copyright Protection Center; app store payment compliance with Apple IAP and Google Play Billing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After setup, the WFOE should implement governance and digital compliance. If operating directly in China, apply to MIIT for the ICP filing or license, and to NPPA for Internet game publishing approval if the virtual slots or social casino game is distributed to Chinese users; confirm that no real-money gambling or prize-redemption mechanics appear in order to comply with PRC gambling prohibitions. Register software copyright with the China Copyright Protection Center for evidence of ownership. For app store distribution, ensure Apple IAP and Google Play Billing are the only payment rails and that targeted age ratings, data privacy policies and responsible gaming controls are published. Maintain compliance records for audits.
required_dossiers: Business license and unified social credit code
Data privacy and user protection policy
Game rules, content description and no-real-money-gambling certification
Responsible gaming and anti-addiction system documents
Annual corporate governance filings and board minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a digital license application is rejected, revise the content to remove gambling-like features, obtain a local legal opinion, and re-file; if foreign ownership restrictions bar an ICP license, restructure through a licensed local publisher or content partner, subject to separate compliance advice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no industrial licensing board is engaged for this pure software publishing activity; if in-China Internet game distribution is contemplated, the relevant digital content authorities are NPPA and MIIT.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial, manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing operating license is required for ISIC 5820 software publishing. If the simulated social casino product is distributed onshore in China, a separate NPPA Internet game publication approval and MIIT ICP license may be required subject to foreign investment restrictions.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Not Applicable. The activity involves no physical construction, no industrial facility, no chemical process, no assembly line and no warehousing operation, so no Environmental Impact Assessment registration or full EIA report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no industrial wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste generation thresholds apply. The only waste streams are ordinary municipal domestic sewage and office solid waste, which are subject to standard city sanitary codes and the local building waste disposal rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no civil defense fire permit, structural load inspection, or high-risk occupational safety approval is required for office-only software publishing. The office landlord should maintain a valid building fire inspection certificate, fire extinguishers, and an evacuation plan, and the WFOE should comply with the general workplace safety obligations of the Work Safety Law for desk-based employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); administered online through the China Electronic Taxpayer (e-Tax) Unified Electronic Taxpayer Service Platform, with local municipal and provincial STA tax service halls for supplementary filings, and the China International Trade Single Window for export customs and foreign-exchange linked tax data
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Obtain the WFOE business license from the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) printed on the license is the legal Tax Identification Number and VAT registration number for all mainland Chinese tax purposes. Step 2: Rely on the automatic one-time SAMR-STA registration data and log in to the local STA e-Tax platform within 30 days to complete the tax registration details, including legal representative identity, financial accounting standard, bank account for tax payment and refund, and expected tax types: Corporate Income Tax, Value-Added Tax, urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, and stamp duty. Step 3: Confirm the VAT taxpayer status in the e-Tax platform: small-scale taxpayer status if annual taxable sales are at or below RMB 5,000,000, or apply for general VAT taxpayer status voluntarily; mandatory general status applies once annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000. Step 4: Record the USCC in every e-invoice, customs declaration, contract, and bank foreign-exchange receipt. Step 5: For a foreign non-resident enterprise without a permanent establishment in China, no separate Chinese tax identification number is ordinarily issued; the domestic withholding agent registers the non-resident enterprise legal name, foreign country tax identification number and address in the e-Tax platform when withholding VAT and Corporate Income Tax on China-source income, including royalties, service fees, dividends or interest
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the WFOE is a Chinese resident enterprise taxed on worldwide Corporate Income Tax; not a pass-through entity; no territorial exemption for foreign income; subject to VAT as an in-scope taxable person; no special tax-exempt zone classification applies
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: China does not provide a US-style check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch entity election; available statutory elections are limited to (a) voluntary registration as a VAT general taxpayer for enterprises below the RMB 5,000,000 small-scale threshold, (b) retention of small-scale taxpayer status where eligible, (c) the election to apply VAT zero-rating or exemption on qualifying cross-border services and exported goods through the e-Tax export-tax-refund module, and (d) the special software VAT treatment under which self-developed software is taxed at 13% with an immediate refund of the VAT paid above 3% of software sales

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) of the People's Republic of China
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Registration as a VAT taxpayer is mandatory at establishment for every mainland enterprise; mandatory general VAT taxpayer status is triggered when annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000. Enterprises below this threshold are classified as small-scale taxpayers, currently with a monthly sales VAT exemption of up to RMB 100,000 where the applicable relief policy remains in force
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory use of the State Taxation Administration Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoice (FDEI) platform: every VAT invoice, credit note and export invoice must be issued through the national e-invoice service platform using the taxpayer digital tax account; each invoice receives a globally unique number, digital anti-fraud QR code, and is transmitted to the STA in near real time via the platform API or enterprise ERP integration. Offline or privately generated invoice numbers are prohibited; voiding, red-letter reversals and export tax-refund supporting invoices must be recorded in the FDEI system and reconciled with the STA digital tax account. Golden Tax Phase IV data analytics automatically detects invoice inconsistency, mismatch of customs declarations, and suspected circular invoicing

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The 0% export VAT rate is available for: (1) tangible goods that are physically exported from mainland China, declared to China Customs under a paperless export customs declaration in the China International Trade Single Window, exported by a VAT general taxpayer, and accompanied by collected export proceeds; and (2) qualifying offshore software services, information system services, and other listed cross-border modern services supplied to overseas purchasers and consumed wholly outside mainland China. For app-store digital games, the WFOE must demonstrate through the Apple App Store Connect or Google Play Console platform sales reports that the end-user customer is located overseas and the game is not consumed in mainland China; the service contract, intellectual-property license, zero-rating declaration in the e-Tax export-tax-refund module, platform payout records, and bank inward remittance evidence must all be consistent with the declared overseas service recipient. Zero-rating is denied if the software or game is sold to a Chinese domestic purchaser or downloaded by a user within mainland China
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: China Customs Export Declaration (paperless export declaration record generated via the China International Trade Single Window; the functional Chinese equivalent of the export bill of entry)
Ocean Bill of Lading, air waybill, or international rail/road waybill evidencing physical cross-border movement
Commercial sales invoice and export sales contract or purchase order

Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) for export proceeds, or the equivalent designated-bank export foreign-exchange receipt confirmation issued under SAFE trade foreign-exchange monitoring, reflecting the overseas purchaser and amount received
Export VAT zero-rating or exemption application record from the STA e-Tax export tax refund module
For digital services, the Apple App Store Connect or Google Play Console platform sales statement proving offshore end users and the corresponding platform payout report
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA may reopen prior export refund declarations in audit; any unsubstantiated, fraudulent, or cyclically invoiced export zero-rating will be disallowed, the VAT refund will be clawed back, output VAT reassessed at 13%, daily late-payment penalties of 0.05% imposed from the date the refund was obtained or tax became due, and an administrative fine of 0.5 to 5 times the underpaid tax may be levied for general underpayment; intentional export VAT refund fraud is subject to a penalty of 1 to 5 times the fraudulently obtained refunded tax. The taxpayer credit rating will be downgraded, future export tax refund eligibility may be suspended, and Customs or criminal authorities will handle cases involving forged customs declarations, false bills of lading, sham foreign exchange receipts, or fictitious cross-border software service contracts, with exposure to fines, confiscation of unlawful gains and custodial penalties under the Criminal Law

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC), through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a rigorous managed-floating exchange-rate system, and the RMB is only partially convertible. Current-account trade in software and digital game publishing services is generally convertible for licensed commercial banks through the SAFE direct reporting system; this requires underlying contracts, invoices, tax records and platform payout statements. Capital-account transactions, including inbound WFOE equity injections, must be channelled through a foreign-invested enterprise capital account after completing FDI registration with SAFE and receiving a bank-issued FDI registration form. Surplus working capital may be retained in a foreign exchange settlement account or converted to RMB at the onshore market rate, but profit remittance and dividend outflows require audited financial statements, tax clearance, and SAFE reporting through the bank. A WFOE may lawfully remit its profit after CIT payments and reserve requirements to the foreign parent, but the procedure entails proof of tax contribution and a written no-objection from the booking bank. In practice, banks require all service export receipts to be supported by invoicing evidence and depersonalised platform payout reports, and there is no free fungibility between a company's domestic RMB cash and offshore CNY or USD balances without a genuine commercial underlying transaction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The statutory regime no longer imposes mandatory conversion; the effective mandatory conversion ratio is zero percent, meaning the WFOE may retain 100% of export receipt FX in a foreign currency settlement account or settle to RMB on a voluntary basis. The repatriation timeline is governed by the contractual payment terms; for software service exports the bookkeeper must evidence collection within the contract settlement date, and if a contract is silent, the prudent safe harbor used by major banks is 180 days from invoice issuance. All export proceeds received into the onshore bank account must be reported to SAFE by the bank through the direct reporting system, and the WFOE must ensure its SAFE business registration is current before the inward remittance is credited.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Foreign Exchange Account and RMB Basic Operational Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Foreign Exchange Account and RMB Basic Operational Currency Account
FDI Capital Foreign Exchange Account and RMB Basic Operational Currency Account
FDI Capital Foreign Exchange Account and RMB Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital-only banks and non-bank EMIs without a PBOC/SAFE banking license are legally barred from opening RMB current accounts or performing domestic clearing for a mainland WFOE. They cannot issue CIP-compliant Chinese payment instructions, hold SAFE registrations, or obtain a CIPS membership. At best, an offshore EMI can only service a holding-company bank account outside China, and all WFOE operating capital, royalties, and local payroll must flow through a licensed PRC commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical appearance of the statutory legal representative is generally mandatory at initial account opening; some tier-1 banks allow a remote video interview if the controller is already a known bank client, but any remote option requires a notarized, apostilled/consular-legalized power of attorney, a passport technical review, a board resolution appointing the resident signatory, and the original enterprise legal personality certificate. The bank will also inspect the registered office lease and require the company chop, and no account is opened until the compliance officer has verified the ultimate principal owner to individual level.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in the UBO chain where the foreign parent is held by corporate shareholders spread across multiple jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate register extracts for each entity in the ownership chain up to the named individual UBOs, passport copies, a group organisational chart, UBO and source-of-funds declarations, audited financial statements for all material shareholders, and bank reference letters from the remitting parent bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Entity engaged in virtual slots/social casino publishing may be misclassified as gambling-related money-laundering exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A licensed PRC legal opinion confirming the product offers no cash-out, no real-money wagering and is a non-gambling simulated entertainment product, full game terms and user agreements, Apple/Google developer contracts, platform payout statements proving revenues are legitimate app-store sales, and an independent AML compliance manual covering user sanctions screening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident legal representative or directors are unable to satisfy in-person identity verification and local presence tests
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized/consular-legalized passport and biographical resume, apostilled power of attorney, a registered-office lease agreement, PRC work/residence permit, board resolution designating specific account signatories, plus certified prior bank reference letters and the entity's tax representative appointment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source and nature of seed capital or initial capital injection is unclear, especially parent-funded loans or IP licensing proceeds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder loan agreements and full lender bank statements, IP assignment/license contracts, SAFE filing receipts for inbound equity or shareholder loans, opening balance-sheet audit, certificate of incorporation and bank statements of the WFOE, plus CIT withholding vouchers for any interest or royalties paid abroad.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital must circulate through the SWIFT network via an MT103 from the parent's bank into the WFOE's dedicated FDI capital account at a licensed domestic bank. The remittance information must state the SAFE foreign-exchange purpose code for foreign direct investment equity injection, the WFOE's SAFE registration number, and the exact company name, and the bank will complete the SAFE FDI registration in the capital account system. Before credit is released, the WFOE must provide the business license, FDI registration form, covenant of source and application, board resolution approving the capital contribution, and an accountant's capital verification report where the bank policy requires it. Once landed, the RMB conversion is conducted at the onshore market rate; the funds must be used in the approved business scope and cannot be temporarily parked in non-operating financial products without SAFE approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound vendor disbursements for software subcontracting, marketing, and licensing are cleared through the same onshore bank using SWIFT MT103 remittances or, if the counterparty is in a country with CIPS access and accepts CNY, through the bank's CIPS channel. The bank requires the underlying services contract, commercial invoice, tax withholding certificate, and SAFE service trade payment declaration. For physical goods purchases, the WFOE may use an irrevocable unconfirmed commercial letter of credit or documentary collections (DP/DA) routed through its correspondent bank to the supplier's presenting bank, with standard Incoterms and shipping documents, though this is not the core theatre of a digital gaming business. For dividend outbound payments, a validated profit resolution, audited financial statements, and tax clearance must accompany the MT103 and the payee must be the registered parent entity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable CNY/USD forward contracts for forecast sales proceeds supported by real current-account exposure, executed with the same PRC bank
Onshore cross-currency swaps for matching the WFOE's long-term foreign-currency capital and interest obligations, subject to SAFE registration and actual exposure tests
Cancellable and non-cancellable forward contracts with periodic mark-to-market margin calls, to hedge invoice receivables under the platform payment rails
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) may be considered only by the offshore parent for CNH positions and are not available to the mainland WFOE for speculative RMB trades

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Information Report (Annual Return) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and local market supervision administration at the district or municipal level
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January through 30 June each year for the immediately preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inclusion in the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations after the statutory deadline; if the omission is not cured within three consecutive years, inclusion in the List of Serious Illegal and Dishonest Enterprises, with restrictions on legal representatives and senior executives, negative market-credit records, and possible administrative cancellation or revocation of the business license for companies becoming inactive without lawful cause.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Information Annual Report (including foreign investor identity, ultimate actual controller, shareholding structure and investment information)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) through the shared SAMR/MOFCOM annual report platform, with data coordination with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January through 30 June each year for the previous calendar year; initial, change and equity-transfer reports must be submitted within 30 days of the relevant corporate event or shareholding change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit or late submission triggers a statutory order to rectify; continued non-payment or non-rectification exposes the WFOE to an administrative fine of RMB 100,000 to RMB 500,000 (approximately USD 14,000 to USD 70,000) under Article 37 of the PRC Foreign Investment Law, plus credit-record impairment and increased regulatory scrutiny.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax (CIT) Settlement Filing and Payment (annual tax reconciliation return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) local competent tax authority in the WFOE jurisdiction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the end of each calendar tax year, i.e. on or before 31 May of the following year, unless an approved extended tax-filing period applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts a daily surcharge of 0.05 percent of the overdue tax; failure to file may attract an administrative fine of RMB 2,000, or RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 for serious non-compliance; fraudulent or evasive filing may attract a penalty of 50 percent to 500 percent of the evaded tax, compulsory tax collection measures, asset freezes or seizures, and criminal referral for serious tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) Stock Equity Registration (annual foreign exchange equity and assets/liabilities confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through the local SAFE branch or the SAFE capital project information system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 June each year, reporting the year-end equity, foreign exchange, asset and shareholding data of the WFOE for the immediately preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or non-filing constitutes a foreign-exchange compliance breach; SAFE may issue a warning and a correction order, suspend foreign-exchange receipt, payment or profit-remittance operations until the registration is regularized, and impose an administrative penalty under the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Foreign Exchange Administration, typically a warning plus a fine of RMB 30,000 to RMB 300,000 depending on the severity of the breach.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory audit report prepared by a licensed Chinese accounting firm and submitted to the shareholders or shareholders meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and company statutory records; the audited financial statements must also be available to SAMR, tax authorities and SAFE upon demand and are relied on for tax and foreign-exchange filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year WFOE, the audit report is to be completed before the annual shareholders meeting and, in practice, before the annual CIT settlement filing deadline of 31 May; ordinarily the audit is completed by 30 April each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to arrange the statutory audit violates PRC Company Law and the PRC Accounting Law; regulators may order correction and impose administrative fines on the company and responsible personnel, tax annual returns may be treated as incomplete or inaccurate, dividend and profit remittance processes may be blocked, and the company may be exposed to negative findings in regulatory audits or annual inspection reviews.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: There is no quantitative balance-sheet, turnover or headcount exemption in China: every PRC-incorporated company, including a wholly foreign-owned enterprise limited-liability company, is statutorily required to engage an accounting firm licensed under PRC law to audit its annual financial report under PRC Company Law Article 164 and the PRC Accounting Law. Even a dormant, zero-revenue or single-shareholder WFOE must prepare and audit statutory financial statements. No asset, revenue or employee threshold triggers or removes the audit obligation. In practice, the audited report is also a precondition for the annual CIT settlement where related-party transactions exist, for SAFE FDI stock equity registration, and for dividend or profit remittance to the foreign shareholder. Transfer-pricing contemporaneous documentation rules under SAT Announcement 42 of 2016 may apply above RMB 200 million for tangible-asset related-party transactions, RMB 100 million for intangible or financial-asset related-party transactions, and RMB 40 million for related-party service transactions, but these thresholds do not replace the universal annual audit mandate.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE/Chinese GAAP), which are substantially converged with IFRS; IFRS as issued by the IASB is not accepted as a substitute for statutory individual financial statements. Qualifying small enterprises may adopt the Ministry of Finance Small Enterprise Accounting Standards, but the WFOE remains subject to statutory annual audit. Statutory financial statements must be prepared in RMB and maintained in Chinese for local filings; foreign-parent IFRS or US-GAAP reports are supplementary only.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: China does not operate a separate annual UBO certificate system; the annual confirmation is embedded in the SAMR/MOFCOM Annual Enterprise Information Report, which requires disclosure of the foreign investor, ultimate actual controller and foreign investment structure. Any shareholding transfer, actual-controller change or modification of registered information must be filed through the SAMR/MOFCOM foreign investment information reporting system within 30 days of the change, and the corresponding company-registration amendment must be filed with SAMR within the same 30-day statutory window. The statutory register of members must be updated concurrently. SAFE requires the annual FDI stock equity registration by 30 June each year. Under PRC anti-money-laundering rules, the WFOE must identify and maintain beneficial-ownership records and update them on an event-driven basis for at least the required retention period, although no public annual UBO filing is made.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders Resolutions and Board Resolutions
Register of Equity Transfers and Pledges

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 to USD 3,000 per year for a basic registered office or secretarial address in most Chinese cities; USD 3,000 to USD 8,000 per year for full corporate secretarial, statutory register maintenance and filing-manager services in Tier-1 cities.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 to USD 10,000 per year for a small or medium WFOE with straightforward digital-game or social-casino operations; USD 10,000 to USD 30,000 per year for a WFOE requiring related-party transaction review, transfer-pricing contemporaneous documentation, or extensive SAFE remittance and foreign-exchange audit support.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Resident WFOEs may access a 15% reduced rate under the High-New Technology Enterprise regime; qualified software enterprises may qualify for the 'two-year exemption and three-year half-rate' incentive from their first profit-making year, producing an effective 0% for the first two years and 12.5% for the next three years; a 100% super-deduction for qualifying research and development expenses is available until at least 2027; tax loss carryforward is statutorily 5 years under the general rule, although qualifying high-tech or technology-oriented small and medium enterprises may carry losses for 10 years in certain circumstances. All incentives require substantive business activity and qualified expenditure within China, not mere contractual arrangements through a shell.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (A-Class) Form A200000, filed through the PRC State Taxation Administration Electronic Tax Bureau (eTax portal), including the related-party transaction reporting schedules and all discretionary incentive forms.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement return, supplemented by quarterly provisional prepayment returns due within 15 days after each quarter-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return and final settlement must be submitted within 5 months after the fiscal year-end, ordinarily 31 May for a calendar-year WFOE; quarterly provisional payments must be filed and paid within 15 days after the close of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating revenue, including gross receipts from simulated social casino game publishing, virtual slot and chip packages, in-app purchases, subscriptions, advertising, and licensing fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A China-incorporated WFOE is a resident taxpayer and must declare worldwide income. Apple IAP and Google Play Billing commissions must not be netted against revenue; report gross platform sales as revenue and the 15%-30% platform commission as a cost or expense. Reconcile platform reports with bank statements to avoid concealed offshore receipts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of operations, including direct game development costs, contracted studio fees, content licensing, server infrastructure, bandwidth, app-store commissions, and payment processing fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to non-resident contractors for services performed wholly outside China may still require VAT withholding or non-resident service income analysis if the service is verifiably sourced in China. Each cross-border payment must be supported by signed agreements, time records, deliverables, and arm's-length pricing evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxes and surcharges, including urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, stamp duty, and property or vehicle taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Value-added tax itself is not deductible in the corporate income tax return; only surcharges economically borne and actually paid are deductible. Verify that all imports of overseas advertising or technology services are documented with VAT withholding vouchers and compliant e-invoices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling and marketing expenses, including user acquisition, app-install campaigns, app-store search ads, influencer payments, and loyalty or free-chip promotions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Marketing services rendered by a related offshore entity must pass TP and economic substance review. A foreign affiliate with no personnel, assets, risk management, or decision-making cannot substantiate a markup. The 6% VAT on imported marketing services and the 10% non-resident income tax on China-source service fees must be properly withheld where chargeable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Administrative expenses, including executive salaries, legal and accounting fees, office rent, group management fees, and intellectual property royalties paid for game software or brand licenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalties paid to non-resident licensors are nominally subject to 10% withholding tax, reduced only when a valid DTA claim is accepted; software royalty characterization requires careful factual analysis between copyright in the software and the copyrighted article. The deduction is disallowed if the royalty is not arm's length, the licensor lacks beneficial ownership, or the arrangement is a conduit for profit repatriation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Finance expenses, including interest on domestic and offshore bank loans, shareholder loans, bond interest, and foreign exchange losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to a non-resident shareholder or affiliated lender carries a 10% statutory withholding tax, subject to treaty reduction. Thin capitalization rules limit deductible interest to a debt-to-equity ratio of 2:1 for the related-party debt; interest treated as excessive is recharacterized as a distribution and is neither deductible nor exempt from WHT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income and expenses, including government grants, fines, donation expenses, asset disposals, and foreign exchange gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Government subsidies must be properly classified as taxable or sanctioned non-taxable income under the enterprise income tax framework; non-compliant fines are non-deductible. Cross-border settlement gains from Apple or Google treasury operations must be disclosed if they represent interest or financing income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total accounting profit before tax, being the sum or net of the above operating, financing, and non-operating items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is only the accounting starting point. The WFOE must reconcile statutory accounting profit to taxable income by applying tax adjustments; no profit-shifting entry made solely through affiliate invoices can reduce this figure in the absence of an arm's-length and substantive business transaction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment increases adding back non-deductible expenditures, excessive related-party payments, thin-capitalization interest, entertainment expenses above statutory caps, and payments lacking proper supporting vouchers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a foreign parent allocates group management fees or royalties but provides no identifiable services or receives only circular cash flows, the tax authority will add back the entire amount under the arm's-length principle and may apply GAAR. The WFOE should attach a full TP documentation package and intercompany flowchart.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment decreases, including tax-exempt dividends received from Chinese resident investees, R&D super-deductions, accelerated depreciation, and deferred revenue adjustments recognized differently for tax purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign dividend income from a treaty jurisdiction may be taxed with a foreign tax credit rather than exempt; claim the RMB super-deduction only for genuinely controlled R&D activities in China. Avoid inflating R&D expenditure by routing routine development fees through offshore shell companies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward offset shown as the utilization of prior-year tax losses against current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The statutory general limit is 5 years for most WFOEs. A loss claimed by a WFOE that acquired an existing company or shell should be examined for continuity of ownership and business. Artificial loss allocation among connected entities to circumvent the 5-year limit is a red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after all adjustments and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any reclassification of deductible royalties or interest as dividends, any CFC inclusion, and any TP adjustment will increase this line. The filed amount becomes the base for the 25% statutory corporate income tax rate before incentive reductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax reductions and exemptions, including the High-New Technology Enterprise 15% rate, software enterprise two-year exemption and three-year half-rate, and small low-profit enterprise preferential calculation where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Each incentive requires formal qualification filing and a substantive factual foundation. A social casino software publisher must demonstrate ownership or core R&D of the game technology, Chinese operational personnel, and qualified revenue; trophy-asset or passive royalty structures will be denied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax payable after reductions, foreign tax credits, and quarterly prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the foreign tax credit separately for foreign-source income using the statutory 'foreign income attributable tax' limitation; no credit is granted for WHT that is genuinely a payment arranged through a conduit or for taxes not actually paid. Ensure bank balance for any refund or shortage is reconciled with eTax records.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing exposes the taxpayer to a fine from RMB 2,000 up to RMB 10,000 under Tax Collection Law Article 62; failure to pay by the statutory deadline triggers a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% under Article 32. Concealment of revenue, falsified books, or fraudulent tax returns attract a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax under Article 63. Criminal tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201 is prosecuted where evasion is relatively large (generally RMB 50,000 or more and more than 10% of the tax payable), resulting in up to 3 years imprisonment; where the evasion is statutorily huge, the responsible persons face 3 to 7 years imprisonment plus fines. Tax authorities may freeze bank accounts, seize assets, and impose exit bans through the Serious Untrustworthy Taxpayer blacklisting mechanism.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding tax on gross dividends distributed by a Chinese resident enterprise to a non-resident corporate shareholder; applicable DTA may reduce the rate to 5% where the beneficial owner is a resident of the treaty jurisdiction and directly holds at least 25% of the WFOE capital, with other treaties providing 10%, 15%, or other agreed percentages.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the foreign shareholder or the WFOE as withholding agent must submit to the PRC tax authority: (1) a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority; (2) a Beneficial Ownership Declaration or equivalent statement; (3) evidence of shareholding ratio and holding period, ordinarily requiring at least 12 months ownership for the lower dividend rate; (4) the dividend distribution resolution and board minutes; (5) audited financial statements or bank settlement evidence; and (6) a statement confirming that the foreign shareholder has no permanent establishment in China to which the dividend income is effectively connected. The reduced WHT should be applied at the time of remittance only after approval or a valid treaty benefit filing; otherwise the statutory 10% must be withheld and a refund may be claimed within 3 years under Tax Collection Law Article 51.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory withholding rate is 10% for both interest and royalties paid to non-resident recipients. DTA rates vary by counterparty, commonly 10%, 7.5%, or 5% for interest and 10%, 7%, or 5% for royalties. Software-related royalty or license payments are closely scrutinized: the transfer of a full copyright attracts royalty treatment, whereas a limited end-user license or shrink-wrap transaction may be treated as business profit without a PE. Separate 6% VAT may also be collected on imported software royalties and service fees through the tax authority.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: RMB 40 million for related-party service transactions; RMB 100 million for intangible-asset or financial-asset related transactions; RMB 200 million for tangible-asset related transactions; with a Master File obligation generally arising when group related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion. A related-party transaction disclosure schedule must accompany the annual return whenever any related-party transaction exists.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Mainland China does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the PRC Corporate Income Tax Law Article 47 and Implementation Regulations Article 120 impose a general anti-avoidance and substance-over-form rule. Tax authorities will disregard contracts that lack business purpose and economic substance, recharacterize pass-through arrangements, and attribute profit according to Core Income-Generating Activities performed in China. A WFOE that keeps development staff, product managers, and strategic decision-makers in China while shifting the resulting profit to a zero-tax offshore affiliate will be adjusted. Controlled Foreign Company rules under Article 45 may also impute undistributed offshore profits where the offshore entity has no real business activities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion through concealed gross receipts and false accounting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The directors instruct finance personnel to record only net Apple IAP/Google Play Billing proceeds instead of gross revenue, maintain undisclosed overseas bank accounts for virtual item sales, omit advertising revenue, or fabricate development expenses to reduce taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Collection Law Article 63 requires payment of the evaded tax plus daily interest at 0.05%, and imposes a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax. Criminal Law Article 201 punishes tax evasion where the amount is relatively large and exceeds 10% of the tax payable with up to 3 years imprisonment; for statutorily huge evasion, the responsible persons face 3 to 7 years imprisonment plus fines. The tax authority may freeze bank accounts, attach assets, and add the entity to the Serious Untrustworthy Taxpayer list.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil liability is imposed under Company Law principles permitting veil piercing where abuse of corporate personality is used to defraud creditors or evade taxes, making directors jointly and severally liable for uncovered tax liabilities and restitution. Directors, the legal representative, and the finance director may be prohibited from leaving China, may have property preserved or seized, and may be criminally prosecuted as directly responsible persons. The personal bank accounts of directors who received the hidden revenue are also traceable and attachable.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Shell-Affiliate Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE sells game software or user rights to a Hong Kong, BVI, or Cayman affiliate at an artificially low price, pays inflated royalties or management fees to a shell parent with no employees or assets, fails to file contemporaneous TP documentation, and then claims treaty benefits on dividend or royalty remittances from that shell.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate Income Tax Law Articles 41, 44 and 48 authorize the tax authority to adjust income under the arm's-length principle, disregard missing documentation and apply reasonable deemed assessments; late-payment interest runs on the adjusted tax. Under Tax Collection Law Articles 24, 35 and 63, failure to keep proper books and deflated related-party income may attract penalties from 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax. The treaty benefit itself will be denied if the offshore recipient is not the beneficial owner or lacks substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly structured the circular payment chain can have the corporate veil pierced, becoming personally liable for restitution of the adjusted tax, interest, and penalties if the arrangement drained the company beyond its ability to pay. They may be blacklisted by name for serious tax violations and denied exit clearance. Criminal prosecution for fraudulent tax returns can follow where the fabricated agreements or invoices were used to hide taxable income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold and Remit Withholding Tax on Outbound Dividends, Interest, and Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE makes dividend distributions to a foreign parent, pays interest to an offshore lender, or pays royalty to a non-resident licensor without withholding the statutory 10% withholding tax, without filing the non-resident withholding return, or without securing an approved DTA reduction and later remits the funds abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Collection Law Article 69 orders the withholding agent to pay the amount that should have been withheld and imposes a penalty ranging from 50% to 300% of the un-withheld amount. The tax authority will also recover the unpaid tax from the non-resident payee where collectable, and late-payment interest applies from the original due date. Unreported outbound payments are additionally subject to foreign exchange audit, administrative fines, and possible criminal tax referral.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and financial officers who sign remittance orders knowing tax was not withheld are exposed to administrative fines, personal joint and several liability where their conduct caused corporate insolvency, travel bans, and inclusion in the tax blacklist. If the unreported foreign remittance was part of a scheme to evade taxes or launder proceeds through offshore accounts, the responsible natural persons face criminal prosecution under Criminal Law Article 201 or money laundering provisions, with custodial sentences and confiscation of personal assets.
